QuestionStmt.S: The change in the internal energy of the mass of gas, when the volume changes from V to 2V at constant pressure P is ($\gamma = \frac{C_p}{C_v}$)

Solution.S:
Change in internal energy: $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$.

Given $\gamma = \frac{C_p}{C_v}$ and $C_p - C_v = R$, so $C_v = \frac{R}{\gamma-1}$.

$\Delta U = n \frac{R}{\gamma-1} \Delta T = \frac{P \Delta V}{\gamma-1}$ (since $P \Delta V = nR \Delta T$ at constant pressure).

$\Delta V = 2V - V = V$, so $\Delta U = \frac{PV}{\gamma-1}$.

Thus the correct option is D.
